en: Mayon volcano has a six-kilometer Permanent Danger Zone to protect people from sudden, deadly lava avalanches.
Coastal towns near the Philippine Trench must maintain clear tsunami evacuation routes because underwater earthquakes trigger huge waves.
Residents living near the Cagayan River during typhoons must evacuate early to avoid dangerous, fast-moving flash floods.
During summer, the extreme heat index in Tuguegarao requires residents to drink extra water to prevent heatstroke.
Stagnant water around Laguna de Bay breeds mosquitoes that transmit dengue fever to nearby communities.
Hikers climbing Mount Pulag must wear thick jackets because temperatures at the summit can drop to near freezing.
People near Taal Volcano must wear N95 masks during eruptions to protect their lungs from toxic ashfall.
Strong rip currents in the West Philippine Sea during the habagat season make swimming extremely dangerous for beachgoers.
Families on the steep slopes of the Cordillera mountains must plant deep-rooted grass to prevent deadly landslides.
The intense ultraviolet radiation at high-altitude locations like Baguio City requires hikers to wear sunscreen to prevent sunburns.
Coastal communities in Eastern Samar must prepare for storm surges because Pacific typhoons bring massive, destructive ocean floods.
Houses built directly above the Valley Fault System in Marikina must be reinforced to survive major earthquakes.
